confounds: Diagnosed users were more active in every fold, so raw post frequency and any-hit prevalence are exposure-sensitive.

Source order lacks reliable timestamps, so block coverage is persistence of language within the retained timeline, not duration or recurrence of a clinical episode.

negative_results: The direct depression-term feature is sparse: self-directed prevalence was 12.3% diagnosed versus 5.0% control, but the median normalized rate was zero in both groups.
Anhedonia, concentration/memory, and guilt/worthlessness lexicons had low coverage or weak separation; broad terms were heavily confounded by ordinary forgetting, insults, and daily-life complaints.

Strict self-harm terms were more prevalent among diagnosed users (13.9% versus 4.5%), but median normalized frequency was zero in both classes, so this is a low-coverage auxiliary flag rather than a robust standalone signal.
Positive language was not depleted; it was common in both classes and somewhat higher among diagnosed users, contradicting a simple negative-affect-only interpretation.
